derivedFrom: the rules in section 7, not from a run. The set of facts a name carries and the source of each are written from the assembler's stated inputs: the last stored session gives four, the indicators give one per name computed on that session, each immediate band gives its two edges and its strength, the ladder gives the trend state, each of the eight stored moves gives three, the swings give a count and the calendar gives the next dated event or says it is not on file. The values are asserted against the stores they were read from rather than against a copy of the payload, so a stage that wrote the wrong number does not agree with itself.
frozen: nothing here is frozen from a run. The payload hash is not stated, because a hash of a payload is a function of that payload and stating it would be a regression baseline wearing the clothes of an expectation.

factsPerName.membershipNote: the company's name the membership row holds, which every fixture name's span states (see the membership expectation's names), so every file carries it: a prompt lists it and a research pass ranks a document whose title names the company by it.
factsPerName.note: ordinal order, which is what the payload is written in: sma200 sorts before sma50 because a string comparison reads the third character and not the number.
factsPerName.movesNote: every move the annotator stores, which is section 17's eight a name, from 6.6: the largest keeps the name it has carried since 5.3 and the other seven are named for their rank, four facts each. They arrived because a local model writing the cause of each move names each move's date, and a date in prose has to be one this file holds. The fourth, the session a move was measured from, arrived later in the same checkpoint, because a cause may rest only on a document published inside the move and a span with one edge holds nothing; each is derived here from the exchange calendar, as the session that many sessions before the one the move ended on, rather than read back off the bars. Every fixture name holds eight moves over its stored year, which is what makes the count per name the same for all four.

properties.everyFactNamesItsSource: a number in written prose must exist here, and the source is what says which stage computed it
properties.namesAreInOrder: the payload is written with the facts in name order, so two runs over one store produce the same bytes and a diff is a difference in the figures rather than in the writing
properties.aNameWithNoBarsGetsNoRow: an absence rather than a file of nulls
properties.aNameWithNoDatedEventSaysSo: not on file, rather than a blank a reader supplies themselves
properties.theChangeListSurvivesAFactsRerun: the two writers own disjoint columns of the same row, and the assembler's statement names two columns and no more

openedName.derivedFrom: worked by hand from the fixture's captured inputs, not from a run. The table growth is read off the captured segment table, segment-report-KEYS-R85.htm, the same way: the company's revenues 1,846 against 1,352, Communications Solutions Group's revenue 1,345 against 940 and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group's 501 against 412, in millions, each group found by the words its fact's name carries because a group's label is the archive's own. The guided figures are the six the claim checker reads in the release's Outlook passage, in the order it states them: revenue of $1.930 billion to $1.950 billion, growth of approximately 37%, earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 and approximately 172 million shares, each a magnitude times the scale its unit word carries; the years the passage names are read as years and are not figures.
